extracted.intended_audience: writers, lecturers, professors, orators, and educators concerned with style and pedagogy
extracted.subtask_short: writing and lecturing: style vs substance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and applying modes of diction (scientific, popular, and fine/ornate) when communicating knowledge to different audiences, and for balancing imagination (taste) with understanding (reason).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste must not encroach on substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste must be confined to regulating the external form, while reason and experience determine the substance and the essence of conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If taste applies to the matter itself (choosing or distorting materials to please the senses), it betrays its mission: 'if it applies this law not only to the operation, but also to the matter itself... the statement is empty.' Keep form subordinate to truth; do not let ornamentation replace logical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use beauty to prepare the mind, not to substitute for proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Gracefulness of clothing can avail little to convince the understanding, but it places us in a favorable attitude to receive truth by charming representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty can excite appetite for knowledge and remove obstacles to attention, yet it cannot replace the need for logical demonstration. Use attractive form to open souls to truth but ensure the contents themselves commend themselves to the understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation in aesthetic ornament when imparting knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Great moderation must always be used; sometimes ornament defeats the end depending on the kind and degree of knowledge aimed at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether ornament helps or hinders the specific instructional goal: for strict scientific conviction, excessive aestheticism may be counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate imagination to understanding in strict reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case where it is essential to carry out a rigidly accurate sequence of reasoning, imagination must forego its capricious character and be made subordinate to the necessity of the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude individual and sensuous elements that would interrupt the logical chain; fashion exposition to 'overthrow this effort of the imagination by the exclusion of all that is individual and sensuous.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose form according to audience capacity and interest
rubrics_metrics.description: When interest or self-denial cannot be relied upon, resign the attempt to impart strictly scientific knowledge and choose a freer, more beautiful form of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the audience lacks attention or background, prefer popular or fine diction to secure reception. Conversely, prefer scientific style when the audience can follow and the proofs are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular instruction: pair ideas with perceptions and cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular speakers and writers should present along with their ideas the perceptions and separate cases to which they relate, leaving the reader's understanding to form conceptions impromptu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix imagination and perception to reproduce familiar representations rather than create new abstractions; this makes ideas immediately graspable for an untrained audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensuous presentation trades generality for vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensuous presentation conceals the general in the particular, giving a living image (entire representation) where attention is concerned with the conception (part-representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such presentation is rich and vivid but limited and poor in scope: it offers a complete single case at the cost of curtailing understanding of the whole sphere. Use when concreteness and immediate appeal matter more than abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific presentation requires strict logical sequence and abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce strict conviction on principles, not only the contents but the mode of stating them must be according to the laws of thought: connected in the same strict logical sequence as in the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid individualizing and sensuous elements; present part-representations and conceptual distinctions clearly so the understanding can reconstruct necessary truths through analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine language employs individualizing and figurative expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal features that contribute to freedom of the imagination are the individualizing of objects and the figurative or inexact expression of a thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use individual cases to represent species and figurative language to associate different ideas subordinate to a higher idea; this gives imagination freedom while the conceptions follow necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for juxtaposition: necessary conceptions with apparently free perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfy the understanding by the closest connection between conceptions (spiritual part) while making perceptions (sensuous part) appear to cohere through arbitrary play of fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'happy relation between external freedom and internal necessity' produces eloquence: logical rigor underlies an appearance of imaginative freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orator's utterances must be self-contained and conclude fully
rubrics_metrics.description: The orator's audience is continually renewed and unprepared; accordingly in every address the orator must finish what he wishes to do and each harangue must form a whole and contain expressly and entirely his conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure speeches so each one delivers a complete, comprehensible argument or appeal without relying on prior lectures or continued attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professor should favor scientific style to build lasting knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The professor ought to endeavor to transmit the full and entire property of the knowledge that he communicates to him; the student accumulates in view of an ulterior end and for a future use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presuppose trained dispositions in students, expose the method and strictness of thought, and encourage exercise of the pure understanding rather than mere aesthetic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid attractive (aesthetic) clothing of scientific matter when teaching youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurtful to choose for the instruction of youth books in which scientific matters are clothed in an attractive style, because it prevents the exercise of pure understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young learners need training in distinguishing form from substance. If you want serious study, present the method and difficulty so students learn to value exertion and analytic thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate taste only after mastery of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: When once the knowledge has been acquired (first point observed), the exercise of taste can have useful results; it is necessary to be quite the master of a truth to abandon without danger the form in which it has been found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let students first grasp concepts firmly under scientific form, then apply aesthetic presentation to restore knowledge to living intuition and make it effective in will and life.

rubrics_metrics.name: True beauty rests on limitation, exact definition, and necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: True beauty reposes on the strictest limitation, on the most exact definition, on the highest and most intimate necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine harmony addresses the entire man and does not show its conformity to law; strive for a unity where form and law appear natural rather than imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of form without substance (cleverness with nothing to express)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form without substance is a shadow of riches, and all possible cleverness in expression is of no use to him who has nothing to express.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not value ornament and wit over thought; cultivate understanding before cultivating mere aesthetic polish to avoid superficial bel-esprit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius/artist must discipline imagination by study and attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: True genius of the artist is recognized by patience defecting all obstacles as regards details; he piles up, grain by grain, the materials of the wonderful structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists and poets must subject imagination to study (e.g., anatomy for painters, inner life for poets) so that spontaneity is supported by rigorous preparation and truth to nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger: refined aestheticism applied to will corrupts morality
rubrics_metrics.description: When the pretensions of aesthetic taste bear on the will, they become pernicious and infallibly deprave the heart; the moral destination of man requires the will be independent of sensuous instincts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow taste to become the supreme lawgiver of conduct; maintain the independence of will and duty from sensuous aesthetic inclinations.
